messages:
erica: quick FYI — during an int8 bake we started seeing malformed JSON in tool-call args when streaming + batch_size > 1. reproducer attached below.

sam: ugh, can you paste the minimal prompt + model variant? is this only int8 or also awq/gptq? :thinking:

erica: repro (super small):
```python
# model: rwd/gpt-small-int8-sampler-v2
prompt = 'CALL_TOOL compute({"values": [1,2,3]})'
resp = model.generate(prompt, stream=True, batch_size=2)
# sometimes the tool args come out as: {"values": [1,2,3
# missing closing bracket, so the tool call parser crashes
```

kai: quick hypothesis: tokenizer splitting across internal batch boundaries scrambles a trailing `]` or a quote, then streaming assembly doesn't re-join correctly. saw similar when we had chunked-kv-cache + continuous-batching on older runtime.

erica: good call. i dug through logs and found consistent pattern: the dropped token is the last byte of the JSON array (usually `]` or `}"`). only shows up on batch_size >=2 with streaming. single-request streaming (batch=1) is fine. non-streaming with batch>1 also fine.

sam: can you dump the raw token ids for a failing case? helps check if tokenizer itself splits the character.

erica: pasted below (ids anonymized):
```
input_ids: [101, 2054, 2036, 102, 4001, 23, 556, 301, 12]
stream_chunks:
  chunk0: [101, 2054, 2036, 102, 4001, 23]
  chunk1: [556, 301, 12]  # last token corresponds to `]` in text form
```

kai: hmm that alignment looks fine. suspect the streaming assembly code that joins chunk0+chunk1 is trimming leading/trailing whitespace or applying a sanitizer that assumes chunks are full tokens. check runtime/stream_assembler.py around join_chunks().

ci-bot: pipeline-run #4021 finished — int8-sampler-v2 functional tests show 7 failures, 5 are "tool-call JSON parse error". link: https://ci.redwood/tests/4021

erica: filing a quick issue and adding logs. tentative mitigation for production: turn off streaming for now on the int8 sampler routing rule and fallback to non-streaming until we patch.

sam: can you add a unit test that forces split-token boundary inside JSON sequences? i'll take the bisect of runtime patches vs tokenization.

erica: yep. i'll add a fuzz case to structured-output tests that simulates token-splitting at arbitrary indices and asserts post-assembly JSON validity.

kai: long-term, we should ensure stream assembler does a JSON-safety check if output mode is structured. e.g. attempt incremental parsing and request a retry or buffer more tokens if partial JSON is detected. also record the percent of streaming toolcalls that required buffering to measure perf impact.

erica: agreed. creating RFC for two fixes: (1) minimal runtime patch (do not strip chunk edges; basic rejoin) + hotfix to routing rules; (2) assembler-level partial-JSON detector + optional buffering.

sam: timeline? can we aim for a hotfix today and a proper PR next week?

erica: hotfix rollout window: canary in west-1 tonight, full rollout tomorrow morning if green. PR for assembler follow-up by EOD Friday.

kai: also add an e2e eval comparing structured-output pass rates across fp16 / fp8 / int8 (current gateways). we need numbers in the RFC so product knows perf vs correctness tradeoff.

erica: will do. adding a note: early numbers show fp16 ~99.8% valid JSON on our eval set, int8 sampler ~96.3% with streaming, int8 non-streaming ~99.5%.

sam: perfect — thanks. i'll pick up the bisect and runtime checks.

erica: thanks team. tagging followups: @eng-runtime for assembler, @eng-ml for evals, @platform for routing change. :white_check_mark:
